answer: Sequential passage attestation. Each identity must complete a randomly routed voyage through three existing agents before activation. En route, it relays a signed payload; every hop and the summit of the route time-log the traversal. An identity reaching the harbor gains standing only if its full path verifies against the route's signatures. Attacker cost is per attempt: fabricating N paths needs N distinct verified relay chains, since a failed route forces a fresh traversal from the start.
